resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register gives a 17-foot open timber tower. A 1942 Coast and Geodetic Survey description gives a wooden structure on eight wooden legs, 30 feet high. A December 1935 newspaper item describes a steel frame 20 feet off the ground. The 30-foot figure is kept as height_m; the disagreement is not resolved.

sources.title: Kettenpom Peak Lookout, Trinity County, California

notes_for_editor: Destruction in the August Complex fires is supported by two independent sources (FFLA chapter report and peakbagging.com). Brief status gone is more specific as destroyed; facts.status uses destroyed, no correction filed. Height is the open question: the Register's 17 feet, the 1942 survey's 30 feet and the 1935 steel frame of 20 feet disagree, and height_m 9.1 follows the survey. The Register and the weebly header use different forest names (Six Rivers now; Trinity National Forest in the older header); the story uses Six Rivers. No staffing source was found, so none is recorded. No photos recorded: the peakbagging page's photos have no license or URL in the cached text. One web search used; it surfaced the peakbagging destruction note and no description of the site after the fire.
